title: [spec-bug] 06-security.md Key Binding check 3 still asserts SAN /128 IID == kid (withdrawn invariant)
description: spec/06-security.md:1162-1164 says: The leaf certificate SAN native /128 has an IID equal to that same kid, per the verifier address-binding check (appendix-x509-cert-profile.md section 8 step 4). But the appendix step 4 requires SAN == upstream AddrForKey(leaf public key) byte-for-byte and explicitly states the SHA-512 IID is not embedded in the routable address and MUST NOT be substituted into its lower 64 bits (appendix lines 102-107, 280-283). The IID-in-address invariant was withdrawn by the settled upstream-yggdrasil-addressing decision (spec/decisions.jsonl); test/vectors/gcp3_trust_models.json already quarantines ygg_addr[8:16]==IID bindings as REJECTED-PROFILE REFERENCE. The 06-security text contradicts both the decision and the appendix it cites. Found during appendix-x509-cert-profile sweep. Suggested fix: reword check 3 to require the SAN native /128 to equal AddrForKey(leaf public key) and drop the IID-equality clause. Label human-only for the wording decision if desired; the address-derivation side itself is settled.
close_reason: Reworded spec/06-security.md Key Binding check 3 (lines 1162-1168): SAN native /128 must equal upstream AddrForKey(leaf public key) byte-for-byte per appendix-x509-cert-profile.md section 8 step 4, with an explicit MUST-reject for SAN entries carrying the kid (SHA-512 IID) in the lower 64 bits. Drops the withdrawn IID-equality clause that contradicted the cited appendix step 4, the same document's own section 8.7 (lines 132/165/166: 'the former lower-64-bits==IID MUST is withdrawn'), spec/decisions.jsonl upstream-yggdrasil-addressing, and test/vectors/gcp3_trust_models.json (quarantines ygg_addr[8:16]==IID as REJECTED-PROFILE). Checks 2/4 untouched — self-referential identity now binds transitively through the leaf pubkey (kid == IID(pubkey) AND SAN == AddrForKey(pubkey)). Codereview 3x delegated to reviewer model: correctness/security/edge-cases all PASS with zero findings. Spec-text-only change; no code tests apply.
